claims.text: The Comptroller's release of November 18th, 2026 carries a headline saying Huffines kills a tax on cloud storage and website hosting. The rule it describes is only proposed.
claims.quote: Comptroller Huffines Kills Tax on Cloud Storage and Website Hosting to Save Texans Money
claims.document: Texas Comptroller, news release, November 18, 2026

claims.text: Texas Comptroller Don Huffines announced the new rules in a release dated November 18th, 2026.
claims.quote: Texas Comptroller Don Huffines today announced new rules confirming that internet hosting,
claims.document: Texas Comptroller, GovDelivery bulletin, November 18, 2026

claims.text: The Comptroller says the proposed rules treat internet hosting, cloud computing and artificial intelligence as hosted technology services that are not taxable data processing.
claims.quote: cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and other hosted technology services are not taxable
claims.document: Texas Comptroller, news release, November 18, 2026

claims.text: The release names the rule being amended as Comptroller Rule 3.308.
claims.quote: Proposed amendments to Rule 3.308
claims.document: Texas Comptroller, news release, November 18, 2026

claims.text: According to the Comptroller, a data processing service under the amendments is one where the provider takes data the customer supplied and hands it back in a usable format.
claims.quote: supplied by the customer and returns it in an organized, usable format
claims.document: Texas Comptroller, news release, November 18, 2026

claims.text: The Comptroller says the amendments also require software sales to be allocated so Texas taxes only the Texas share.
claims.quote: require that software sales be allocated so Texas taxes only the portion
claims.document: Texas Comptroller, news release, November 18, 2026

claims.text: Huffines said the Legislature taxed data processing in 1987.
claims.quote: The Legislature taxed data processing in 1987,
claims.document: Texas Comptroller, news release, November 18, 2026

claims.text: Huffines said the Legislature never taxed artificial intelligence.
claims.quote: It did not tax artificial intelligence.
claims.document: Texas Comptroller, news release, November 18, 2026

claims.text: The release said the proposed rule would appear in an upcoming issue of the Texas Register.
claims.quote: The proposed rule will be published in an upcoming issue of the Texas Register.
claims.document: Texas Comptroller, news release, November 18, 2026

claims.text: The Texas Tribune reported on November 19th, 2026 that the limit would cost the state $18 billion over six years, based on the Comptroller's own estimates.
claims.quote: will amount to an $18 billion loss over the next six years
claims.document: The Texas Tribune, November 19, 2026

claims.text: The Tribune reported that local government tax losses would total $4.67 billion over the same period.
claims.quote: Tax revenue losses for local governments will total $4.67 billion in that time.
claims.document: The Texas Tribune, November 19, 2026

claims.text: The Tribune reported that the Comptroller's agency projects a $1.9 billion loss in state general revenue.
claims.quote: His agency projects losses of $1.9 billion in state general revenue
claims.document: The Texas Tribune, November 19, 2026

claims.text: The Tribune reported nearly $600 million in lost local sales tax revenue in the first year.
claims.quote: nearly $600 million in local sales tax revenue
claims.document: The Texas Tribune, November 19, 2026

claims.text: The Tribune reported that by fiscal year 2032 the state would lose $4.3 billion and local governments about $1.1 billion.
claims.quote: By fiscal year 2032, the state will lose $4.3 billion and local governments about $1.1 billion, according to the estimates.
claims.document: The Texas Tribune, November 19, 2026

claims.text: Comptroller-elect Sarah Eckhardt asked Huffines in a letter of November 9th to stop pursuing every rule change begun since August 1st.
claims.quote: Eckhardt in a Nov. 9 letter asked Huffines to cease pursuit of all rule changes initiated since Aug. 1
claims.document: The Texas Tribune, November 19, 2026

claims.text: The Tribune describes Huffines as having lost his election this month.
claims.quote: Comptroller-elect Sarah Eckhardt asked Don Huffines, who lost election this month, to cease policy changes
claims.document: The Texas Tribune, November 19, 2026

claims.text: Eckhardt is set to take over the comptroller's office on January 1st, according to the Tribune.
claims.quote: prepares to assume control of the office on Jan. 1
claims.document: The Texas Tribune, November 19, 2026

claims.text: Huffines replied that he would keep making rules until he leaves office.
claims.quote: he would not cease rulemaking until he leaves office
claims.document: The Texas Tribune, November 19, 2026

claims.text: The Tribune reported December 20th as the earliest date the rule could be adopted.
claims.quote: The earliest possible adoption would be Dec. 20
claims.document: The Texas Tribune, November 19, 2026

claims.text: The Comptroller's proposal says it would clarify what a data processing service is and confirm that internet hosting and other hosted technology services are not taxable.
claims.quote: to confirm that Internet hosting and other hosted technology services are not data processing services and are not taxable under Tax Code, §151.0101(a).
claims.document: Texas Register, Comptroller of Public Accounts, proposed amendments to 34 TAC §3.308, TRD-202604746

claims.text: The Comptroller concludes the agency's earlier reading of the data processing tax was too expansive.
claims.quote: concludes that the interpretation was too expansive.
claims.document: Texas Register, Comptroller of Public Accounts, proposed amendments to 34 TAC §3.308, TRD-202604746

claims.text: Under the proposed definition, a data processing service processes data the customer supplied and returns it to the customer in the format the customer asked for.
claims.quote: defines a data processing service as one in which the provider processes data supplied by the customer and returns that data to the customer in an organized and usable format requested by the customer.
claims.document: Texas Register, Comptroller of Public Accounts, proposed amendments to 34 TAC §3.308, TRD-202604746

claims.text: Storing or manipulating data would not by itself be a data processing service.
claims.quote: The storage or manipulation of data, standing alone, is not a data processing service.
claims.document: Texas Register, Comptroller of Public Accounts, proposed amendments to 34 TAC §3.308, TRD-202604746

claims.text: A customer using a provider's software or computing to process its own data would not be a data processing service either.
claims.quote: including the customer's use of a provider's software, platform, or computing resources to process the customer's own data, is not a data processing service.
claims.document: Texas Register, Comptroller of Public Accounts, proposed amendments to 34 TAC §3.308, TRD-202604746

claims.text: The proposal defines hosted technology service to include cloud computing, artificial intelligence and quantum computing.
claims.quote: New subsection (a)(5) defines hosted technology services, including cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and quantum computing.
claims.document: Texas Register, Comptroller of Public Accounts, proposed amendments to 34 TAC §3.308, TRD-202604746

claims.text: The fiscal note puts the loss to the state's General Revenue Fund at $1,947,310,000 in fiscal year 2027.
claims.quote: would result in losses to General Revenue Fund 0001 of $1,947,310,000 in fiscal year 2027
claims.document: Texas Register, Comptroller of Public Accounts, proposed amendments to 34 TAC §3.308, TRD-202604746

claims.document: Texas Register, Comptroller of Public Accounts, proposed amendments to 34 TAC §3.308, TRD-202604746

claims.quote: Losses to units of local governments, including municipalities, counties, and transit authorities would be $507,450,000 in fiscal year 2027

claims.document: Texas Register, Comptroller of Public Accounts, proposed amendments to 34 TAC §3.308, TRD-202604746

claims.document: Texas Register, Comptroller of Public Accounts, proposed amendments to 34 TAC §3.308, TRD-202604746

claims.text: The chief revenue estimator found the amended rule will have an insignificant effect on the state's economy.
claims.quote: will have insignificant effect on this state's economy.
claims.document: Texas Register, Comptroller of Public Accounts, proposed amendments to 34 TAC §3.308, TRD-202604746

claims.text: Comments go to Robin Robinson, the Associate Deputy Comptroller for Tax, by mail or by email.
